name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28H disrupts the IP6-dependent PH-TH homodimer of BTK. Histidine at position 28 cannot make the contacts the arginine makes across the dimer interface, so the dimer does not form and BTK activation at the membrane is impaired.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E6", "E8", "E1", "E2", "E9"], "would_refute": "Modelled or experimental PH-TH dimer structures place residue 28 with no atom within contact distance (about 4 \u00c5) of the partner chain, and the R28H model keeps the interface buried area and interface energy within the wild-type range.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "E6 reports that this exact substitution impairs activation by preventing PH-TH dimerization, and E8 ties the dimer to the same R28H effect. Both are about R28H itself, so they outrank the general support. Still missing: no dimer structure carrying R28H (G3) and no experimental dimer measurement."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28H removes a side-chain contact that BTK's PH domain uses to bind the inositol phosphate head group (IP4 or IP6). arguments: {"statement": "R28H destabilises the PH domain fold, through loss of buried packing or a polar network near residue 28, so the domain is partly unfolded or underexpressed.
